pages.title: Home
pages.description: Brookside Neighbours is a fictional community charity used to demonstrate the Polysite nonprofit theme.

blocks.heading: A street is only as strong as the neighbours on it.
blocks.subheading: We run a food share, a community garden, a repair cafe and shared lunches, all by and for the people who live here.
blocks.alt: An illustrated street of houses with a community garden of raised beds, a tree and neighbours standing together

items.heading: The food share
items.body: Fresh and tinned food, free to anyone who needs it, no questions asked. Open three mornings a week.

items.heading: The community garden
items.body: Sixty-two raised beds, tended by neighbours of every age. Half of what grows goes to the food share.

items.heading: The repair cafe
items.body: Bring a broken lamp, toaster or jumper. Volunteers fix it with you, and teach you how.

items.heading: Shared lunches
items.body: A long table, a hot meal and company, every Thursday. Come on your own and leave with friends.

items.heading: Homework club
items.body: After-school help for children aged 7 to 14, run by retired teachers and keen teenagers.

items.heading: Neighbour check-ins
items.body: A friendly phone call or visit for people who live alone, from someone who lives nearby.

blocks.name: Marguerite Osei

blocks.quote: It started with one pot of soup on a Thursday. What keeps it going is that everybody gives a little, and nobody has to give a lot.

items.quote: I came for the food share and stayed for the Thursday lunch. I have not eaten alone on a Thursday since.
items.name: Ruth Adair

items.quote: I fixed my first toaster here. Now I run the Saturday bench.
items.name: Mo Hussein

items.quote: My grandchildren know the names of every vegetable in the garden. So do I, now.

pages.title: Our work
pages.description: The food share, the garden, the repair cafe and shared lunches.

blocks.heading: Four things, done with care
blocks.body: Everything we do is run by volunteers and paid for by small gifts. Nothing has a waiting list, a form to prove need, or a fee.

pages.title: Get involved
pages.description: Volunteer with Brookside Neighbours: sign up here.

blocks.heading: An hour a week changes a lot
blocks.body:
You do not need experience, only a bit of time. We will pair you with someone who has done the job before and make sure you always know who to ask.

Most volunteers come once a week for two hours. Some come once a month. Both are welcome.

items.question: Do I need a background check?
items.answer: Only for the homework club and neighbour check-ins. We arrange it and pay for it.

items.question: Can I bring my teenager?
items.answer: Yes. Under-16s come with an adult, and older teenagers are some of our best volunteers.

items.question: What if I can only help occasionally?
items.answer: That is fine. Tell us in the form and we will call you for one-off jobs like garden days and big lunches.

pages.title: Donate
pages.description: Give to Brookside Neighbours. A demonstration page: no payment is taken.

blocks.heading: Where your gift goes
blocks.body:
This is a demonstration site, so no payment is taken here. On a real charity's site this page would link to its payment provider.

For the story: $10 buys 25 meals for the food share, $25 stocks a repair bench for a month, $50 plants and waters a garden bed for a year and $100 hosts a shared lunch for forty people.

items.heading: Nine in every ten dollars goes to the work
items.body: The rest keeps the lights on and the books honest.

items.heading: We publish our accounts
items.body: Every spring, in plain language, on this site.

items.heading: You can stop at any time
items.body: Change or cancel a regular gift with one email.

pages.title: About us
pages.description: The story and the people of Brookside Neighbours (all fictional).

blocks.heading: How it started
blocks.body:
In the winter of 2011 Marguerite put a pot of soup on a table outside the old school hall and told a few people. Twelve came the first week.

Today three hundred volunteers keep four projects running. We are still based in the same hall, and the soup is still on the first Thursday of every month.
